reviewed_by: Codex focused Core tool and built-in MCP failure review
reason: Exercise the shared failure envelope across actual fixed command, gateway, Notebook, and Security Tools declarations; Butler capability refusals; brokered chat and mission failed-receipt handoff; real gateway MCP dispatch; bounded retrieval queries and Work conflicts; MCP grants and built-in runtime prerequisites. The six selected feature-specific Python files collect 132 tests.
exclusions: No full suites. UI, frontend, Playwright, native, and low-level MCP framing tests are not selected because the change is confined to Core-owned tool-error classification and provider/harness result handoff; it does not change browser controls, layout, or MCP wire framing. A disposable authenticated source Core with synthetic data and an inert provider exercised the actual LAN chat API: a rejected Notebook read delivered usage and recovery to the next model request, followed by a successful Notebook list. Browser journeys are not selected because there is no UI or browser-state change. No live provider, live Core deployment, or physical device is involved.
